purpose: Read-only source discovery and public map/service review for the exact ranked city record; no globals/runtime/catalog integration.
assessment: The ranked WUP point is a settlement centroid, not an official boundary or parcel identity. The normal Topovision public layer list shows imagery and municipal limits and omits the cadastral WFS layer; the city GeoServer nevertheless publicly exposes it. Research queried only the safe `id` attribute plus geometry. Sampled polygon geometry is evidence of nearby cadastral mapping, not a title determination or citywide coverage claim. No owner/address fields were requested or retained.
registryAssessment: The municipal Topovision is an official city GIS, and the municipality’s cadastral technical service procedure handles cadastral/lot-related certifications. Its public GeoServer WFS capabilities expose the city cadastral lot feature type `SaoGoncalo:lote_a_cadastro_sg`; bounded anonymous geometry queries and full adapter qualification returned parcel polygons near the ranked locator.

searchQueries.query: São Gonçalo Rio de Janeiro official cadastral parcel map public GIS WFS municipal lot layer
searchQueries.scope: Identify official city cadastral/registry sources and public parcel geometry.
searchQueries.result: Official city Topovision and municipal cadastral technical-service sources were found. Topovision’s default layers show orthophotos and municipal limits; its public GeoServer WFS exposes a cadastral lot layer. Bounded WFS queries returned polygons near the WUP point.
searchQueries.executionMethod: Separate English web search, public viewer/config inspection, WFS GetCapabilities/DescribeFeatureType and bounded geometry-only requests.

officialSources.observation: Official municipal Topovision GIS. Its visible/configured public layer list contains orthophoto/imagery and municipal boundary layers; it does not list the cadastral lots exposed directly by the WFS.
City Hall map and neighborhood page; supports local municipal mapping context.
Municipal form for the technical cadastre subsecretariat includes lot/legalization/parceling/certification procedures.
Public GeoServer WFS capabilities list cadastral layers including SaoGoncalo:lote_a_cadastro_sg; no account or token was used.
Layer schema exposes safe numeric `id`, polygon `geom`, and `lote`; the research request selected only `id` and geometry.
Public WFS endpoint used for bounded 13-cell geometry queries, capped pages, fresh exact-ID reads, explicit absence, footprint lookup and binding.

viewerAndServiceTrace.publicViewerBundle: Viewer HTML / bundled scripts inspected; standard startup layer list exposed orthophoto imagery and municipal boundary only.
viewerAndServiceTrace.queryMode: WFS 2.0.0; CRS:84 bbox; response in EPSG:4326; geometry-only plus id; page-size test 3; no login/token.

qualifier.qa: Independent GEOS 3.14.1 check: 90/90 polygons valid, all Polygon, non-empty; metric areas 320.9589–28692.3464 m². Full QA geometries remained in /tmp; up to three ID-plus-polygon samples are included in the companion GeoJSON.

geometryDecision: The exact WUP-point probe was empty. A bounded 13-cell adapter qualification returned 90 unique nearby lot polygons; all 20 tests passed, including forced three-row paging, 90 fresh-ID reads, explicit absence, footprint lookup and binding. GEOS 3.14.1 validates all 90 polygons. Three safe id-plus-geometry samples are retained. Citywide and exact-point coverage remain unverified.

nativeAndTransportIdentity.freshLookup: Exact native-id queries for all 90 IDs returned identical geometry hashes. Example id 1039986 matches hash e706eb9878bbc63ecc0def0e001cd7026117cd305d89e55cef1083ee430addec.
nativeAndTransportIdentity.transportFeatureId: GeoServer/WFS feature.id varies across viewport and exact-ID reads; not used as parcel identity.
nativeAndTransportIdentity.persistenceLimit: Native numeric id was stable during this run; provider long-term permanence semantics undocumented.

runtimeAssessment.scope: 90 independently audited nearby parcel geometries; no exact WUP point or municipality-wide completeness claim.
